The calibration stack operates under dual paradigms: probabilistic forecasting for binary outcomes using Platt/PAVA/EB-τ, and quantile regression for numeric lines. The EB-τ hierarchical model stabilizes estimates via normal priors on group-level effects, clamped to prevent extreme variance. Conformal abstention ensures that predictions are only made when confidence thresholds are met, avoiding overconfident errors. Stationary bootstrap addresses temporal dependencies by resampling contiguous blocks, enabling robust uncertainty bands. These primitives interlock: EB-τ feeds into Brier/ECE for eligibility, which then informs conformal abstention and bootstrap-based CI estimation. Failure modes include misalignment between calibration and coverage, or instability in τ̂ due to insufficient data.
